newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end stronger after steady U.S. rates.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end stronger after steady U.S. rates.

text.p: Toronto's stock market rose nearly one percent by Tuesday's close as many investors breathed a sigh of relief that the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) did not hike interest rates.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index climbed 60.49 points to reach 6715.81.
"Basically it was the FOMC meeting," said Maison Placements Canada President John Ing. "The classic rates worries are going out the window."

Analysts had expected short-term rates to remain unchanged but the confirmation boosted North American equities markets. Wall Street jumped 115 points to 7918 by day's end. Tuesday's gains in Toronto helped wipe away Monday's 40-point losses and some of Friday's 72-point drop.
"The correction was but one day and here we go again," Ing said.
Trading was heavy at 97 million shares worth C$1.8 billion ($1.3 billion).
All but two of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes finished stronger. Conglomerates soared by more than 2.5 percent, followed by interest-sensitive banks and utilities.
Weak golds and real estate helped rein in gains.
Advancing issues outnumbered declines 568 to 411 and another 301 ended steady.
In individual issues, takeover target London Insurance Group Inc. jumped 6.60 to 33.65 and led most actives at nearly 6.3 million shares.

Great-West Lifeco Inc. announced a surprise C$2.9 billion ($2.1 billion) bid for London Insurance early on Tuesday, topping a C$2.4 billion ($1.7 billion) offer made by the Royal Bank of Canada in June.
Trilon Financial Corp. later said it will tender its 57-percent stake in London Insurance to Great-West Lifeco if Royal Bank does not match the offer.
Industrial products firm Bombardier Inc. fell 1.70 to 27.85 in brisk trading after it reported second-quarter earnings dipped to C$0.24 from year-ago C$0.25.
